proof:
Source: steps 5–9 of the parent's supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1: summation of the deformed pieces (17)–(19), the identity (20)–(21), and the support and mass statements (22)–(25), chapter-06.txt lines 1775–1838), with the deformed pieces V_j = push(φ_j, W_j), H_j, Y_j, E′_j, L′_j, K_j of the parent replaced by abstract sequences satisfying the identities the parent derives for them. Siblings used: TEL = cmcsdtd_hasSum_telescoping_eq_zero (key telescoping_real); ME = cmcsdtd_mass_controls_eval (key mass_eval), applied with U := ℝ^P in degrees m and m + 1. Throughout, δ in a mass bound means ENNReal.ofReal δ, which is < ∞; for a test form ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P), dω := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k ω, so that ∂X(ω) = X(dω) and (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω) hold definitionally.
1. (Mass series.) Termwise comparison (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum) and pulling out the constant (ENNReal.tsum_mul_left) give Σ_j M(V_j) ≤ Σ_j a_j, Σ_j M(H_j) ≤ Σ_j δ·a_j = δ·Σ_j a_j, Σ_j M(Y_j) ≤ Σ_j b_j and Σ_j M(E′_j) ≤ δ·Σ_j b_j. All four are finite, because Σ a_j, Σ b_j < ∞ and δ < ∞ (ENNReal.mul_lt_top).
2. (Remainders.) 0 ≤ M(L′_j) ≤ c_j with c_j → 0, and 0 ≤ M(K_j) ≤ δ·c_j with δ·c_j → δ·0 = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, using δ ≠ ∞). By the squeeze theorem in [0, ∞] (tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le), M(L′_j) → 0 and M(K_j) → 0.
3. (The three limits.) IMS with k := m and the sequence (V_j) (finite mass series by step 1) gives Q₀ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with HasSum (V_j(ω))_j (Q₀(ω)) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P), M(Q₀) ≤ Σ_j M(V_j) ≤ Σ_j a_j, spt Q₀ ⊆ closure ⋃_j spt V_j ⊆ K₁ (⋃_j spt V_j ⊆ K₁ and K₁ is closed; closure_minimal), and Q₀ integer multiplicity because every V_j is. IMS with k := m + 1 and (H_j) (degree (m + 1) + 1 = m + 2) gives R₁ ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) with HasSum (H_j(ζ))_j (R₁(ζ)) for every ζ ∈ 𝒟^{m+2}(ℝ^P), M(R₁) ≤ Σ_j M(H_j) ≤ δ·Σ_j a_j, spt R₁ ⊆ K₂, and R₁ integer multiplicity. IMS with k := m and (E′_j) gives S₁ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with HasSum (E′_j(ω))_j (S₁(ω)), M(S₁) ≤ δ·Σ_j b_j and spt S₁ ⊆ K₃.
4. (T − Q₀ − S₁ = ∂R₁.) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) and put α_j := W_j(ω) − V_j(ω) − E′_j(ω) − H_j(dω). From the hypothesis HasSum (W_j(ω)) (T(ω)) and step 3 (with ζ := dω), HasSum (α_j)_j (T(ω) − Q₀(ω) − S₁(ω) − R₁(dω)) (HasSum.sub three times). Evaluating (I1) at ω gives W_0(ω) − V_0(ω) − (E′_0(ω) − K_0(ω)) = H_0(dω), i.e. α_0 = −K_0(ω); evaluating (I2) at ω gives W_{j+1}(ω) − V_{j+1}(ω) − (E′_{j+1}(ω) − (K_{j+1}(ω) − K_j(ω))) = H_{j+1}(dω), i.e. α_{j+1} = K_j(ω) − K_{j+1}(ω). By step 2 and ME (i) (degree m + 1), K_j(ω) → 0. TEL with a := α and k := (K_j(ω))_j gives T(ω) − Q₀(ω) − S₁(ω) − R₁(dω) = 0, i.e. (T − Q₀ − S₁)(ω) = R₁(dω) = ∂R₁(ω). As ω is arbitrary, T − Q₀ − S₁ = ∂R₁ (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
5. (∂Q₀ is the weak sum of the Y_j.) Fix η ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P). By step 1 and ME (ii)(a) (degree m), the series Σ_j Y_j(η) is summable; let y := Σ_j Y_j(η), so HasSum (Y_j(η))_j y. By step 3 with ω := dη, HasSum (V_j(dη))_j (Q₀(dη)); hence β_j := V_j(dη) − Y_j(η) satisfies HasSum (β_j)_j (Q₀(dη) − y) (HasSum.sub). Evaluating (I3) and (I4) at η gives V_0(dη) = Y_0(η) − L′_0(η) and V_{j+1}(dη) = Y_{j+1}(η) − (L′_{j+1}(η) − L′_j(η)), i.e. β_0 = −L′_0(η) and β_{j+1} = L′_j(η) − L′_{j+1}(η). By step 2 and ME (i) (degree m), L′_j(η) → 0. TEL gives Q₀(dη) − y = 0. Hence ∂Q₀(η) = Q₀(dη) = y, and HasSum (Y_j(η))_j (∂Q₀(η)).
6. (Mass of ∂Q₀.) By step 5 and ME (ii)(b) (degree m, with X_j := Y_j, Y := ∂Q₀, and Σ_j M(Y_j) < ∞ by step 1), M(∂Q₀) ≤ Σ_j M(Y_j) ≤ Σ_j b_j.
7. (Support of ∂Q₀.) Let η ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport η disjoint from K₃. For every j, spt Y_j ⊆ K₃, so tsupport η is disjoint from spt Y_j and (VO) gives Y_j(η) = 0. By step 5 the series of zeros has sum ∂Q₀(η), so ∂Q₀(η) = 0 (uniqueness of sums: HasSum.unique with hasSum_zero). By (S-i) with E := K₃ (closed) and X := ∂Q₀, spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ K₃.
8. (Conclusion.) Q₀, R₁, S₁ satisfy: Q₀ and R₁ are integer multiplicity (step 3); T − Q₀ − S₁ = ∂R₁ (step 4); spt Q₀ ⊆ K₁, spt R₁ ⊆ K₂ and spt S₁ ⊆ K₃ (step 3), spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ K₃ (step 7); M(Q₀) ≤ Σ_j a_j, M(R₁) ≤ δ·Σ_j a_j and M(S₁) ≤ δ·Σ_j b_j (step 3), M(∂Q₀) ≤ Σ_j b_j (step 6). ∎
